structure: A mandatory; B one of two structured; C one of two structured

items.prompt_en: Define a shortage in a market.
requirements_en: State an accurate definition using quantity demanded and quantity supplied at a particular price.

items.prompt_en: Using the source, calculate the weekly shortage of vegetables at the maximum price in thousands of kilograms. Show your working.
requirements_en: Choose the appropriate source figures.
Show the calculation and report the requested unit.

items.prompt_en: Explain, with reference to a correctly labelled demand-and-supply diagram where useful, how the fungal disease could affect the equilibrium price and quantity of vegetables if demand were unchanged.
requirements_en: Explain an adverse production shock with demand held constant.
Explain the direction of the changes in equilibrium price and quantity.
If using a diagram, label axes and initial/new market curves.

items.prompt_en: Analyse two reasons why a maximum price set below equilibrium might fail to improve the actual availability of vegetables.
requirements_en: Develop two economically distinct reasons rather than simply listing them.
Link each reason to market incentives, imbalance and actual availability.

items.prompt_en: Explain why a fall in the inflation rate from 8% to 6% does not necessarily mean that the overall consumer price level is falling.
requirements_en: Distinguish a change in inflation from a decline in the overall price level.
Use the stated rates accurately and recognise the difference between one product price and the consumer price index.

items.prompt_en: Evaluate whether removing the vegetable price ceiling would necessarily benefit low-income households.
requirements_en: Consider benefits from improved supply and access.
Consider changes in affordability and distribution.
Reach a conditional judgement linked to market responsiveness and household circumstances.

items.prompt_en: Explain factors affecting the price elasticity of supply of an agricultural product.
requirements_en: Explain what price elasticity of supply measures.
Develop mechanisms involving production time, spare capacity, storability and resource availability.
Apply the explanation to agriculture.

items.prompt_en: Assess whether a producer subsidy is always more effective than a maximum price in making essential food affordable.
requirements_en: Explain possible changes in supply, prices and affordability under a producer subsidy.
Contrast with the effects of a binding maximum price.
Evaluate costs, market response, distribution and conditions before a judgement.

items.prompt_en: Explain how cross elasticity of demand differs for substitutes and complements.
requirements_en: Define and interpret cross elasticity of demand.
Distinguish substitutes from complements using suitable relationships and examples.

items.prompt_en: Assess whether knowing price elasticity of demand is sufficient for a government to predict revenue from an indirect tax.
requirements_en: Explain the relevance of demand responsiveness to indirect-tax outcomes.
Analyse other relevant determinants including the tax rate, traded quantity and supply response.
Evaluate whether PED alone is sufficient.

items.prompt_en: Explain how an increase in government expenditure can influence aggregate demand and output.
requirements_en: Identify the aggregate-demand channel affected by government expenditure.
Develop the link to output, considering spare capacity and multiplier conditions.
Use appropriate economic terms or a clear AD/AS diagram where relevant.

items.prompt_en: Assess whether supply-side measures are likely to be more effective than a rise in government spending in improving economic growth.
requirements_en: Explain distinct mechanisms of demand-side and supply-side measures.
Compare short- and longer-term output effects and implementation constraints.
Reach a conditional judgement reflecting economic circumstances.

items.prompt_en: Explain two causes of a current account deficit.
requirements_en: Explain the meaning and relevant components of the current account.
Develop two distinct economic mechanisms that may cause a deficit.

items.prompt_en: Assess the effectiveness of an exchange-rate depreciation in reducing a persistent current account deficit.
requirements_en: Explain possible effects of depreciation on export/import competitiveness and values.
Analyse price elasticities, time lags and imported production inputs.
Evaluate when depreciation may or may not reduce the deficit.
